To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we proposed a model for PV panels that can be used to simulate the energy produced by a PV system in a real building, and we validated the model by comparing it with data collected from a real building.

(i) the proposed model is accurate, fast, and easy to implement; (ii) it can be built by solely exploiting the information available in PV panel datasheets; and (iii) it allows to estimate the PV system performance in real time.
a compact PV model is proposed that can be used to predict the power generated by PV arrays in smart buildings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of methodologies for the early design of PV systems for autonomous buildings, by proposing a compact model that can be easily implemented in the EDA flow for smart cyber-physical systems.
the design of methodologies for the early design and performance estimation of PV systems, with the goal of enabling the design of zero-energy buildings.

the development of methodologies and tools that allow for the design of zero-energy buildings by means of a cyber-physical systems approach, where the design is driven by the effective exploitation of renewable energy sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model is a good compromise between accuracy, computational complexity, and the information needed to build it.
the proposed model is able to accurately estimate the PV panel production, while being fast enough to be integrated in a cyber-physical system.
the proposed methodology can be used as a fast tool for PV system design and optimization, and that it can be integrated within the EDA framework to support the design of autonomous buildings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a model for PV panels that is fast and accurate, and that does not require any additional information other than the one available in the datasheet.
the proposed model allows to predict the PV panel output power with an average relative error of less than 3.8%, with a computation time of less than 0.01 seconds.
we have developed a compact PV panel model for Cyber-Physical System in Smart Cities, that is suitable for real time estimation of the performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a compact and accurate model can be built by means of a simple and effective methodology, thus enabling fast and accurate simulations of PV systems.
the model can be used in the early stages of the building design to estimate the performance of PV systems and to optimize the building design accordingly.
the proposed methodology can be used to design and optimize PV systems in smart cities, and in particular in autonomous zero-energy buildings, in which the PV panel is the main source of energy.
